tagline: More freight, thinner profit, a rival mega-merger, and coal fading.

kpis.l: Union Pacific–Norfolk Southern deal on the table

lead_thesis: BNSF's trains are fuller but its profit per haul is shrinking: costs grew faster than revenue, a rival merger could redraw the map, and coal keeps fading.
lead_support: Operating ratio means cost as a share of revenue — lower is better. The fix starts with per-route cost and demand forecasts, not new locomotives.

problems.heading: Revenue rose 15% but costs rose 16% — profit per haul shrank
problems.fact: Volume grew 7% to 2.5M units and the operating ratio still worsened 0.6 points; fuel hit $1.2B and pay $1.4B.

calls.heading: Show cost per carload on every corridor
Fix the worst 10% fuel-burning trains
calls.sub: Makeup, speed and idling — attack the tail.

calls.heading: Freeze capex until cost per carload falls
Pay crews a share of fuel saved

problems.heading: An $85B rival merger could redraw every BNSF route
problems.fact: The Surface Transportation Board set a schedule in August 2026 and denied quick-kill motions in September; BNSF is pressing for access conditions.

calls.heading: Build the traffic-diversion model
calls.sub: Know which lanes flee, gateway by gateway.

calls.heading: Price the 20 gateways that matter most
calls.sub: Revenue at stake, lane by lane.

calls.heading: Offer shippers binding access guarantees
calls.sub: Win customers before the merger closes.

calls.heading: Propose an open-access alliance
calls.sub: Turn a defensive fight into a new network.

problems.heading: Coal volume fell 8% — the only shrinking business
problems.fact: Retirements and cheap gas drove the drop; coal revenue still rose 1% to $722M on price, while intermodal grew 9%.

calls.heading: Date every coal plant's closure
calls.sub: Treat shutdowns like churn — plant by plant.

calls.heading: Move hoppers and crews to intermodal now
Reprice coal contracts with minimum volumes
calls.sub: Get paid when plants run less.

calls.heading: Build rail links for AI data centers
calls.sub: New heavy freight: power, fuel, equipment.

booth.say: BNSF's problem is speed of information: costs, competitors and coal shift faster than the plan.
ask: How do you see cost per carload today — network average or per train?
Where does BNSF's coal forecast live, and who updates it?
